headline: Mandatory Ferry and Seaplane Transportation Booking
reservation: Reach the park by reserved concession ferry or seaplane, private vessel, or permitted tour operator. Campers cannot travel by seaplane; reserve limited ferry camping transport well ahead. Regular Garden Key campsites for up to six people are first come, first served on arrival, with camping fees paid on the island; large groups of 10–20 require advance park reservations.

days.title: Fortress in the Gulf
days.start: Suggested: 7 AM at the Key West Ferry Terminal

stops.name: Fort Jefferson
stops.detail: Tour the massive 19th-century coastal fortress and learn about its role as a Civil War prison.

stops.name: Moat Wall Walk
stops.detail: Walk the perimeter of the fort to see the engineering of the sea wall and clear turquoise waters.

days.driving: Allow 2.5 hours by ferry or 40 minutes by seaplane; maritime conditions vary.
days.note: There are no stores or water on the island; you must bring all food and drink.

days.title: Coral Reefs and Marine Life
days.start: Suggested: 9 AM from the Garden Key Dock

stops.name: South Coaling Dock Ruins
stops.detail: Snorkel around the submerged pilings to see vibrant corals and schools of tropical fish.

stops.name: Garden Key Beaches
stops.detail: Swim in the protected shallow waters or relax on the remote white sands near the fort walls.

days.driving: Walking only; the entire developed area of Garden Key is accessible on foot.
days.note: Use only reef-safe sunscreen to protect the delicate marine ecosystem.

days.title: Avian Observation and Isolation
days.start: Suggested: 8 AM from the Fort Jefferson Parade Ground

stops.name: Bush Key
stops.detail: Observe nesting Sooty Terns and Brown Noddies from the boundary line (seasonal closures apply).

stops.name: Fort Jefferson Ramparts
stops.detail: Walk the upper level for bird's-eye views of the surrounding keys and the vast Gulf of Mexico.

days.driving: Walking only; Bush Key access is strictly limited to the shoreline path when open.
days.note: Bush Key is seasonally closed for nesting; check current status at the Visitor Center.

intel.title: Key West Terminal Logistics
intel.text: Parking in downtown Key West is expensive and limited. Use long-term municipal lots or hotel parking and arrive at the ferry terminal at least 60 minutes before departure.

intel.title: Complete Digital Disconnection
intel.text: There is no cell service or public Wi-Fi on Garden Key. Inform others of your itinerary before leaving the mainland and carry physical copies of permits.

intel.title: Personal Hydration Requirements
intel.text: The park provides no fresh water. Day visitors must utilize ferry supplies; campers must carry a minimum of two gallons per person per day.

intel.title: Transportation Windows
intel.text: Ferry and seaplane schedules are strictly fixed. Missing the afternoon departure requires an emergency stay; check-in times at Key West are firm.

intel.title: Marine Weather Impact
intel.text: High winds and rough seas can lead to same-day cancellations of all transport. Winter cold fronts and summer tropical systems frequently alter the schedule.

plan.arrival: Fly into Key West International Airport (EYW). Stay in Key West the night before your trip to ensure an on-time morning arrival at the dock.
plan.vehicle: No vehicles are permitted in the park; transportation is by boat or seaplane only.
plan.goldenHour: The fort's western ramparts for sunset, available exclusively to permitted overnight campers after the ferry departs.
